Outcome 1: Citizens, especially women and youth in selected counties, are better informed and active in making demands for improved service delivery and for accountability of elected officials on election campaign promises in Liberia.
Outcome 2: Local government officials are more responsive to the needs of citizens, especially women and youth, in the use of social development funds to enhance local development within selected counties.
Outcome 3: Citizens have increased access to justice in rural communities through understanding of their rights and responsibilities, and duties within the justice systems, legal support for engagement, and improved collaboration and partnership amongst the justice systems and beneficiary communities.
Outcome 4: Naymote has increased capacity and effective governance to accomplish its strategic plan for 20262030 and enhance organizational effectiveness to advance/impact democratic governance in Liberia and the ECOWAS subregion.

The proposed contribution 'Democracy Advancement Program (DAP) is a project by Naymote Partners for Democratic Development (Naymote) covering the period 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2025 with a total contribution of SEK 12 000 000. The project has an overall goal 'To enhance democratic governance for inclusive development in Liberia and has a specific objective to increase demand on the government to deliver on its political, development and campaign promises. The project aims to deliver the following three outcomes: Outcome 1: Citizens, especially women and youth in selected counties are better informed and active in making demands for improved service delivery and for accountability of elected officials on elections promises in Liberia. Outcome 2: Local government officials are more responsive to the needs of citizens, especially women and youth in the use of social development funds to enhance local development within selected counties. Outcome 3: Naymote has increased capacity to accomplish it strategic plan 2020-2025 and enhance organizational effectiveness to advance/impact democratic governance in Liberia and the ECOWAS sub-region

"Democratic Advancement Program (DAP)" är ett projekt av Naymote Partners for Democratic Development (Naymote). Insatsen ska implementeras under perioden 1 september 2022 till 31 augusti 2025 med en total budget på 12 000 000 SEK. Projektets övergripnade mål är att förbättra demokratiskt styre för en inkluderande utveckling i Liberia. Vidare är ett specifikt mål att öka allmänhetens krav på regeringen att leva upp till sina politiska löften. Projektet syftar till att uppfylla följande: Resultat 1: Medborgare, särskilt kvinnor och ungdomar i utvalda regioner, är bättre informerade och mer aktiva när det gäller att ställa krav på förbättrade samhällstjänster samt att hålla valda företrädare ansvariga för sina vallöften. Resultat 2: Lokala regeringsföreträdare är mer lyhörda till medborgares, främst kvinnors och ungdomars, behov gällande användning av "Social Development Funds" för att förbättra lokal utveckling inom utvalda regioner. Resultat 3: Naymote har ökad kapacitet att genomföra sin strategiska plan 2020-2025 samt har förbättrad organisatorisk effektivitet för att främja/påverka demokratiskt styre i Liberia och inom ECOWAS-regionen.

description.narrative:
The following results could be seen in the second year (1 September 2023 to 31 August 2024):
Young Political Leadership School Africa (YPLS): -Trained 100 participants in its 11th cohort, raising the total number of alumni to 1,130. -Achieved notable alumni successes, including elected and appointed positions across Africa.
Presidential Performance Tracking: -Monitored 119 promises made by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., reporting 3% completed, 59% ongoing, 14% not started, and 24% unrated due to insufficient data. -The report engaged over 100,000 citizens through diverse platforms, sparking broad discussions and influencing government priorities under the ARREST agenda.
Legislative Performance Monitoring: -Documented 122 legislative sittings, 12 laws passed, and 893 executive officials confirmed. -Enhanced legislative openness by training staff, resulting in improved documentation and tracking. -Engaged the Speaker of the House for reforms, including plans for audits and improved legislative performance.
Citizen Engagement: -Conducted 14 town hall meetings across five counties, reaching 3,753 participants (53% female). This surpassed the 2025 target of 3,145 participants, demonstrating increased public awareness.
Policy Work: -Produced and distributed policy briefs on health and education financing, prompting advocacy for budgetary improvements. -Released 50 ARREST Agenda budget analyses and county service center surveys, fueling informed discussions on government accountability.
Institutional Strengthening: -Released a County Service Center assessment, prompting government action to allocate 40% of revenue for operational improvements. -Developed fundraising and sustainability strategies, enhanced gender inclusion, and secured resources for improved program delivery.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
